traits.note: Standley and Steyermark (1952), Flora of Guatemala III p. 338, genus Hedyosmum: trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious, each inflorescence of one sex; male flowers in spikes, without a perianth, each one anther; the female flower's perianth a tube joined to the ovary with a very short 3-toothed limb. Flora of China vol. 4 p. 138 says the same. Read as perianth usually absent (the many male flowers) and sometimes tepals (the few female ones).
